questions.explanation:
## Why This Question Is Asked
This tests practical policy design, edge-case handling, and CI integration for Kubernetes manifests in a multi-team environment. Candidates must demonstrate understanding of resource isolation, pod hardening, network security, and hardware scheduling constraints.

## Key Concepts
- **ResourceQuota and LimitRange**: Prevent resource starvation and enforce default resource requests/limits per namespace
- **Pod securityContext**: Enforce runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem, and capability dropping for workload hardening
- **Ingress TLS with cert-manager**: Ensure encrypted external traffic with automated certificate management
- **GPU scheduling constraints**: Use nodeSelector and resource requests to restrict GPU workloads to approved namespaces and nodes
- **CI validation**: Integrate Kyverno/OPA Gatekeeper with kubectl dry-run for pre-merge enforcement

## Code Example
```yaml
# Kyverno ClusterPolicy for ML Platform Gates
apiVersion: kyverno.io/v1
kind: ClusterPolicy
metadata:
  name: enforce-ml-platform-gates
spec:
  validationFailureAction: enforce
  rules:
    - name: require-resource-quota
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Namespace]
      validate:
        message: "Each namespace must have a ResourceQuota."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              quota-ready: "true"

    - name: require-security-context
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      validate:
        message: "Containers must run as non-root with read-only filesystem and drop ALL capabilities."
        pattern:
          spec:
            containers:
              - securityContext:
                  runAsNonRoot: true
                  readOnlyRootFilesystem: true
                  capabilities:
                    drop: [ALL]

    - name: require-ingress-tls
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Ingress]
      validate:
        message: "Ingress must use TLS with cert-manager annotation."
        pattern:
          metadata:
            annotations:
              (cert-manager.io/cluster-issuer): "?*"
          spec:
            tls:
              - secretName: "?*"

    - name: gpu-in-approved-namespaces
      match:
        resources:
          kinds: [Pod]
      preconditions:
        - key: "nvidia.com/gpu"
          operator: In
          value: ["1", "2", "4"]
      validate:
        message: "GPU pods are only allowed in approved namespaces with nvidia nodeSelector."
        pattern:
          spec:
            nodeSelector:
              nvidia.com/gpu: "?*"
```

## Verification Strategy

**Local Testing:**
```bash
# Install Kyverno
kubectl apply -f policy.yaml

# Dry-run validate manifests
kubectl apply --dry-run=server -f manifest.yaml

# Test policy against sample manifests
kyverno apply policy.yaml --manifest manifest.yaml
```

**CI Integration (GitHub Actions):**
```yaml
name: Manifest Validation
on: [pull_request]
jobs:
  validate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Validate with Kyverno
        run: |
          kyverno apply cluster-policy.yaml \
            --manifest manifests/ \
            --policy-report \
            --fail-only-on-exists
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Immutability of container images is a core security practice. This checks a tangible gating mechanism candidates can implement in a simple CI step.

## Key Concepts

- YAML manifest parsing
- Image digest pinning (immutable refs)
- Lightweight CI scripts in GitHub Actions
- Local verification parity with CI

## Code Example

```yaml
# .github/workflows/pin-digest.yml
name: Pin Image Digests
on:
  push:
    paths:
      - '**/*.yaml'
      - '**/*.yml'
jobs:
  digest_check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v3
      - name: Install jq and yq
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y jq wget
      - name: Install yq
        run: wget -qO- https://github.com/mikefarah/yq/releases/download/v4.25.1/yq_linux_amd64 -O /usr/bin/yq && chmod +x /usr/bin/yq
      - name: Validate image digests
        run: |
          DIGESTED=$(yq -r '.. | .image? // empty' **/*.yaml **/*.yml | grep -v '^$' )
          if echo "$DIGESTED" | grep -vq '@sha256:'; then
            echo "Found image refs without digest:";
            echo "$DIGESTED"; exit 1;
          fi
          echo "All images pinned to digests."
```

## Why This Is Asked

Tests ability to combine supply-chain security (cosign, SBOM) with policy-as-code (OPA Gatekeeper) in a multi-tenant, regulated context. Demonstrates end-to-end thinking from CI to runtime admission.

## Key Concepts

- Image signing and verification (cosign, public key management)
- SBOM generation and ingest (CycloneDX)
- Policy-as-code (OPA Gatekeeper ConstraintTemplates and Constraints)
- Namespace labeling and non-root container policies
- CI integration and runtime verification

## Code Example

```yaml
apiVersion: templates.gatekeeper.sh/v1beta1
kind: ConstraintTemplate
metadata:
  name: k8simage signing
spec:
  crd: {}
  targets:
  - [' admission.k8s.gatekeeper.sh','' ]
  rego: |
    package gatekeeper.image_signing
    violation["Image is not signed"] {
      input.review.kind.kind == "Deployment"
      not input.review.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].image | image_signing.sign
    }
```

```yaml

apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment

  name: payments-service
  namespace: prod
spec:
  template:
    spec:
      containers:
      - name: app
        image: registry.example.com/payments-service@sha256:abc123...
        securityContext:
          runAsNonRoot: true
```

```yaml

spec:

        securityContext:
```

## Why This Is Asked

Real-world cross-cloud serverless platforms demand automated image signing and artifact attestations. This question tests end-to-end workflow design, policy enforcement decisions, and practical CI/CD integration skills.

## Key Concepts

- Cosign signing and verification
- Rekor attestations for transparency and auditability
- SBOM generation (using tools like Syft)
- Multi-cloud serverless deployment patterns
- GitHub Actions workflow integration

## Code Example

```yaml
name: cks-serverless-sign
on:
  pull_request:
    types: [opened, synchronize]

jobs:
  gate:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Install cosign
        uses: sigstore/cosign-installer@v3

      - name: Set up Syft for SBOM
        uses: anchore/syft-action@v1

      - name: Build and push image
        run: |
          docker build -t ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} .
          docker push ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Generate SBOM
        run: |
          syft ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }} -o cyclonedx-json > sbom.json

      - name: Sign image with cosign
        run: |
          cosign sign --key cosign.key ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Verify signature
        run: |
          cosign verify --key cosign.pub ${{ vars.REGISTRY }}/serverless-fn:${{ github.sha }}

      - name: Upload to Rekor
        run: |
          cosign upload blob -f attestation.json
```

## Failing Manifest (Unsigned Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:abc123
```

## Passing Manifest (Signed Image)

```yaml
apiVersion: v1
kind: Pod
metadata:
  name: serverless-workload
spec:
  containers:
  - name: function
    image: registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
    imagePullPolicy: Always
```

## Local Verification

```bash
# Verify image signature
cosign verify --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256

# Verify attestation
cosign verify-attestation --type cyclonedx --key cosign.pub registry.example.com/serverless-fn:signed-sha256
```

## CI Verification Steps

1. Add Cosign verification step in CI pipeline
2. Block deployment if signature verification fails
3. Verify SBOM matches image contents
4. Check Rekor transparency log for attestation

```yaml
# istio-authz.yaml
apiVersion: security.istio.io/v1beta1
kind: AuthorizationPolicy
metadata:
  name: data-lake-access
  namespace: data-platform
spec:
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: data-lake-gateway
  rules:
  - from:
    - source:
        principals: ["spiffe://data-platform/data-service"]
    to:
    - operation:
        methods: ["GET", "POST"]
        paths: ["/v1/tables/*"]
```

### 4. OPA Policy Example
```rego
#.rego
package kubernetes.admission

deny[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Pod"
  input.request.namespace == "restricted"
  not input.request.object.spec.securityContext.runAsNonRoot
  msg = "Pods must run as non-root"
}

allow[msg] {
  input.request.kind.kind == "Deployment"
  input.request.object.spec.template.spec.containers[_].securityContext.privileged
  msg = "Privileged containers not allowed"
}
```

### 5. CI Enforcement Check
```yaml
# .github/workflows/security-scan.yml
name: Security Scan
on: [push, pull_request]
jobs:
  opa-check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Run OPA policy check
        run: |
          opa eval --fail-defined-deny \
            --data policy.rego \
            --input manifests/
```

## Key Takeaways
- SPIRE provides cryptographically secure workload identity
- Vault enables dynamic secret rotation without application changes
- Istio mTLS ensures service-to-service encryption
- OPA/Rego enforces admission control and runtime policies
